newsitem.title: USA: Crestar sees $50-$55 mln charge for merger.
newsitem.headline: Crestar sees $50-$55 mln charge for merger.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp said on Monday its shareholders and Citizens Bancorp shareholders approved Crestar's acquisition of Citizens, but it would take a $50 million to $55 million pretax one-time charge for expenses related to the transaction.

The company, which said the acquisition would become effective on Tuesday, said it expected its fourth quarter earnings, exclusive of merger-related charges, to be line with analysts estimates. It said the consensus estimate for the fourth quarter was $1.36 per share.
Under terms of the deal announced in September, Crestar said Citizens shareholders would receive 0.835 shares of Crestar common stock for each share of Citizens held.
Crestar said Citizens Bank's business, accounts, facilities and other operations would be consolidated into Crestar's in March, as planned.
Until then, Citizens Bank would continue to operate under its existing name as a wholly owned unit of Crestar Financial, it said.
Based on third quarter financial data, Crestar said its acquisition of Citizens increased its total assets by 23 percent to $22.4 billion.
